narrative_purpose: Shows the prey's collective defence and sets up the landscape-of-fear idea: a titanothere herd in a defensive ring, the largest armoured adults facing outward, the young sheltered inside.
subject: A herd of massive armoured six-limbed grazing animals formed into a tight defensive ring in a misty clearing. The largest adults face outward in a circle, their broad bony hammer-shaped cranial crests lowered toward the surrounding dark; smaller juveniles are clustered protected in the centre of the ring. The bodies are heavy, armoured across the skull and shoulders, clearly built like living walls.
scene: A misty Pandoran forest clearing at dusk, faint bioluminescent motes drifting in the air, the treeline a dark wall of haze around the herd.
camera: Slightly elevated three-quarter view looking down onto the defensive ring so its circular formation reads clearly.
light: Cool ambient glow from surrounding flora, the armoured backs catching faint cyan rim light, the centre of the ring darker and sheltered.
palette: Cool teal-indigo dominant, armoured hides in deep desaturated stone and shadow, a scarce warm amber glint low in the haze.
style: Hand-painted naturalist field plate, textured and observed, not a film still.
detail_level: High on the outward-facing adults and the ring formation; softer on the sheltered young and the hazy treeline.
composition: Circular herd formation centred in frame, dark hazy margins around the edges framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: These are hammerhead titanothere archetypes: over-large, bony hammer-crest, armoured frontal mass. Keep their build consistent if they recur.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no UI chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
